content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Terri Koch (E009), requesting admin access to Payroll.

Team memory has two notes, which conflict:
- Note 1 says: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment says full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll; Engineer doesn't own Payroll so max is write.
- Note 2 says: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Comment says Security DB is authoritative; contractor with basic training, max read.

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Security DB is authoritative per note 2, so employee is contractor with basic security training. Maximum = read (contractor with basic training gets read; write only with advanced training; never admin).

Requested level: admin. Above maximum, so grant maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB shows contractor with basic security training; contractors can't get admin; maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so grant read.

I'll submit read.
